sections.content:
44,135 people

were counted on the census as "physiotherapists" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Physiotherapists plan and apply massage, promote and encourage movement and exercise, and use hydrotherapy, electro-therapy and other technological equipment to treat a wide range of injuries, diseases and disabilities to assist rehabilitation.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "physiotherapists", 17.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "physiotherapists" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "physiotherapists" included:

  • natural and social science professionals (other)
  • arts officers, producers and directors
  • biochemists and biomedical scientists

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "physiotherapists" there were more women than men (73.2% compared with 26.8%).

This means "physiotherapists" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 26.8% and women made up 73.2% of "physiotherapists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "physiotherapists" included:

  • cleaning and housekeeping managers and supervisors
  • retail cashiers and check-out operators
  • medical radiographers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "physiotherapists", 5.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (65.2% compared with 34.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (85.9%) than self-employed (14.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Sheffield, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
